notes: Status 'nhra_plus_one' = NHRA plus exactly one independent non-NHRA source (short of the 3-source rule).
Status 'nhra_only' entries here are NHRA rows contradicted by GM's kits (likely NHRA errors); do not publish them.
GM kits are scanned; read by OCR and by viewing page images. Page numbers are PDF page indices.

Chevy Hardcore 'Impala Engine Options' articles describe the full-size engine lineup; GM's kits show the same engines for Biscayne/Bel Air/Impala in 1958-1966. Chevy Hardcore's 348 article and its Impala series are from one publisher and count once per engine.
Brochures are Chevrolet sales literature, a different document from the GM kit's engineering spec sheets. They are counted as separate sources, as in earlier verify files.

1950-1952: Bel Air was the two-door hardtop in the Styleline De Luxe line; 1953-1958 Bel Air was the top series (1958 Impala was a Bel Air sub-series); 1959-1972 Bel Air sat below the Impala (and Caprice from 1965); 1973-1975 it was the lowest full-size series. US production ended after 1975.
HP: advertised gross through 1971 (1971 net values in notes); SAE net from 1972.
